q: Why do neural networks need non-linear activation functions?
a: Without them, stacked linear layers collapse into one linear layer: \(W_2(W_1x+b_1)+b_2 = W'x+b'\). The network could only learn linear boundaries, no matter how deep. Non-linearities let each layer bend the representation so later layers can separate patterns that weren't linearly separable.

q: How many parameters does a dense layer from 512 to 256 units have?
A single neuron with a sigmoid activation is equivalent to which classical model?
a: Logistic regression: \(\sigma(w^\top x + b)\), trained with binary cross-entropy. A neural network can be seen as many logistic-regression-like units composed in layers.

q: What does the universal approximation theorem say, and what doesn't it say?
a: A network with one hidden layer, a non-linear activation and enough units can approximate any continuous function on a compact domain arbitrarily well. It doesn't say how many units are needed, that gradient descent will find the weights, or that the result will generalise. Deep networks are used because they represent many functions far more efficiently than wide shallow ones.

Batch: the examples used for one gradient update. Iteration (step): one forward + backward + update on one batch. Epoch: one full pass over the training data. 10,000 rows with batch size 100 → 100 iterations per epoch.

q: When would you use a neural network instead of XGBoost?
a: Unstructured data (images, audio, text), very large datasets, multimodal inputs, when you need learned representations or end-to-end training, or sequence modelling. For typical tabular data with moderate size, gradient boosting usually wins with less tuning.

q: Why do deep networks work better than very wide shallow ones in practice?
a: Depth lets the network compose features hierarchically and reuse them (edges → textures → parts → objects), which can represent complex functions with exponentially fewer units than a single wide layer. Shallow networks can approximate the same functions in theory but may need impractically many neurons.
